style.vernacular: Low-rise Pacific island town: single- and two-storey painted concrete-block and timber buildings with hip or gable roofs of corrugated metal in red, green and galvanised grey; whitewashed LMS-era mission churches and college buildings; open verandahs and louvres; coastal ring road lined with palms, hibiscus and frangipani on grass verges, lagoon and forested volcanic hills behind.
style.ornament: Whitewashed church walls with arched windows and small belfries; timber verandahs with simple railings; louvred windows; woven-pandanus and thatch (kikau) roofs at tourist huts; painted shopfront signs in tropical teal, coral and blue; flagpoles in front of government buildings.

sources.what: LMS missionaries made Avarua their headquarters from 1823; tropical rainforest climate; commercial and government centre
palm-studded beaches, forested interior hills, Ara Tapu coastal ring road, churches
